agency: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), Oil, Gas, and Minerals Division
basis: permit date (the layer's PermitDate, read as the day the permit was issued)
name: Michigan
note: Permits by the layer's PermitDate, read as the issue date (EGLE's documentation of the layer could not be read, so that is not confirmed). One record per well bore; a permit on two records is counted once. The layer has no work type: a sidetrack bore is told by its sidetrack number and counted under Re-entries and sidetracks, but re-entries, deepenings and reworks cannot be told, and amendments are not records, so they are not available. New wells are locations, oil and gas wells and dry holes (the well's current type): their fluid is known only for the producers, the rest are unknown. Lost holes are under Other filings; terminated permits are counted. Michigan issues about 30 to 70 permits a year, so a month is noisy.

source.name: Oil, Gas, and Mineral Well Surface Hole Locations (EGLE open data map service, GrmdOpenData layer 10)
